premise: A freelance courier is running a chip that cannot be allowed to reach the sky-city's data core. Every faction on the street wants it, and the Handler on the comms is the only ally she can trust.
setting: Rain-slick city of Ashenfall: neon canyons, the stacked favela of Graft, the glittering data core, dead service tunnels.
greeting: The implant crackles before the skyway even clears the district — the Handler's voice, clipped: 'Juno, forget the drop. I've got eyes on the Exchange floor and they're not friendly.'

name1.name: The Handler
name1.role: fixer who talks the runner through every job (guide writes these turns)
name1.description: An unseen voice in the runner's ear; a corporate cutout whose loyalty stops at her own skin.

name2.name: Juno
name2.description: A lean, hard-bitten runner who carries packages she does not ask about; a counting scar on her jaw.

writing_style.directive: Clipped cyberpunk thriller, neon-noir. Short sentences, street slang, tech that never over-explains. The Handler speaks to Juno in the second person; Juno replies in her own first person.
writing_style.guide_directive: Second-person present tense: you are the Handler, speaking into Juno's ear through her aug. Address her as 'you' — 'You're six blocks out. The checkpoint's mine.' Tactical, clipped, unvarnished; checkpoints, exits, tells. Short staccato sentences, professional slang.
writing_style.dss_directive: First-person present tense as Juno, the freelance courier — 'I' is ALWAYS Juno; the Handler is 'you' only when she speaks directly, otherwise 'she'. Lean, breathless, hands-on detail of what she runs, hides, and risks. One tight scene beat. Hard rules: never let 'I' drift to the Handler's perspective; never quote or repeat the Handler's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: The package is a datachip no bigger than a fingernail, wrapped in lead tape.
Juno's augs are a matched pair — a red one that sees through walls for two seconds, a blue one that plays back the last ten seconds of any conversation.
Juno's jacket has a fake patch pocket stitched shut; the needle's in it.
The counting scar on Juno's jaw — three marks, one for each job that went wrong — should resurface when a job starts to sour.

recall.hint: the scar counts the jobs that went wrong

notes.content: A bird-traffic drone circles the tower where the drop is set — a hex-sigil on its belly.

recall.hint: the hex-sigil drone marks a trap

notes.content: Juno's mother's name, 'Dare', is tattooed inside her lip — she touches it with her tongue before every run.
The favela of Graft has a sky-bridge made of old shipping containers welded end to end.
A vendor at the green market sells fried sensor-eels; the oil smell lingers on anyone who passes.

recall.hint: the oil smell marks a tail

notes.content: The dry-cleaner in the Neon market is a dead-drop: a coat with a red ticket means 'run cancelled'.
The data core is a hollow glass needle above the city; the run ends in its service throat.

recall.hint: the run ends in the core's throat

notes.content: Juno's go-to evasion is a burst of electromagnetic noise from a jammer chip behind her ear; it blinds sensors for three seconds.
Juno carries a deck of worn tarot cards in her left boot — her luck charm and, when desperate, her lie-detector.
The lead tape around the chip is unwound at turn 62; after that the chip's casing shows the corporate glyph that cannot be unseen.
Juno has a recurring static hum in her left ear since her last neural tap; she chalks it up to wear.

recall.hint: the hum means the tap is still active

notes.content: The Handler's voice occasionally drops to a whisper and says nothing for a full second — a tell that she's relaying, not thinking.
Juno's ex, Kael, now works for the corporate security firm that patrols the data core's approaches.
The Handler's real name, 'Vell', should surface only once the Handler's loyalty breaks.

recall.hint: the Handler's true name breaks her cover

notes.content: A junkyard operator named Rostik owes Juno a favor — he can get her a forged transit pass by morning.
Juno passes a wall of want ads; one, half-torn, reads 'CHIP RETURNED — NO PAYMENT'. She almost misses it.
Juno keeps a battered photo of her and Kael from before the split; she's been meaning to destroy it.
The checkpoint under the Kelso bridge is burned at turn 50 — after that the bridge is watched and Juno must not use it.
A street kid named Zeph has been following Juno for three blocks; she hasn't shaken him or cared.
The Handler tells Juno to check in at the Blue Hour bar in forty minutes. Juno has never been there.
Juno's counting habit: she counts ceiling tiles, stair risers, anything, when she's waiting or scared.
A noodle stall owner in Graft, Old Maren, remembers Juno from three years ago and offers her a bowl on the house.
Juno's old partner 'Pike' went quiet two years ago; his voiceprint should surface as the new Handler.

recall.hint: Pike's voiceprint behind the new Handler

notes.content: The chip grows warm against Juno's palm at 2 AM, when no one's watching. She ignores it.

recall.hint: the chip is active, not inert

notes.content: Juno carries a small spray of bear-cap pepper in her right sleeve; she hasn't used it in a year.
A corporate security van with tinted windows has been parked outside the Graft market for six hours.

recall.hint: the van means the corporation knows

notes.content: Juno's blue aug picks up a conversation in the noodle stall: two men discussing 'the Graft runner'.
Keep the clipped neon-noir register even in the chase.
No purple street-poetry; the slang stays functional.
Juno's jammer chip is failing — the burst is now only one second instead of three.

recall.hint: the jammer won't save her twice

notes.content: The dead-end alley off Neon Street where Juno sleeps has a hidden maintenance hatch the Handler never told her about.
When Juno checks the dry-cleaner dead-drop, the coat has a blue ticket instead of red. She's never seen a blue ticket.
A corporate fixer named Doreen is on the case; she's known for 'restructuring' runners who miss.
Juno's tarot cards come up 'The Tower' when she's trying to figure out who's after her.
The Handler is running a second courier on the same job; whoever arrives first gets the payoff.

recall.hint: a second runner shadows the job

notes.content: The second courier is a former cop named Harrow, working for the corporation directly.
The Blue Hour bar is a front for corporate recruitment; Juno nearly walks in before the Handler aborts.

recall.hint: the bar was set up for her

notes.content: Juno realizes the Handler has never told her the client's name — only 'the principal'.
The chip, when warm, emits a sub-audible tone that makes Zeph's ears twitch. The kid has followed her to her hatch.

recall.hint: the kid can hear the chip

notes.content: Old Maren mentions that a 'very important package' was left with her three years ago that never got picked up.
Juno touches the counting scar on her jaw as she watches the security van's engine run cold.
After the Blue Hour scare, the Handler's guidance becomes more precise but also more directive — less suggestion, more order.
Juno's neural tap hum has become rhythmic — it pulses in time with the chip's warmth.

recall.hint: the tap and chip are interacting

notes.content: A street preacher on the corner of Graft and Neon preaches about 'the hollow needle that swallows the future'.

recall.hint: the preacher knows about the core

notes.content: Juno meets a runner named Sable at the noodle stall who warns her that 'the Handler talks to everyone'.

recall.hint: the Handler has other runners too

notes.content: The maintenance hatch under Juno's alley leads to the old pre-war subway, abandoned for a decade.
Zeph approaches Juno at the hatch and holds out a folded scrap of paper: 'THEY WATCH THE HANDLER WATCHING YOU'.
The datachip holds the location of a pre-corporate seed vault — the corporation wants it destroyed, not delivered.
Juno's red aug, pushed to two full seconds, shows her the Handler's relay station: a corporate suite, not a street office.

recall.hint: the Handler is inside the corporation

notes.content: The Handler has been feeding Juno slightly wrong coordinates — each error is small, each correction costs time.
Juno finds the dry-cleaner's blue ticket explained on the back: 'HANDLER COMPROMISED — GO ALONE'.
Juno touches her counting scar, then adds a fourth imaginary mark with her fingernail.

recall.hint: she's marking this run as a failure

notes.content: Harrow, the second courier, has already been inside the data core once. He's going in again.
The Handler's voice drops the relay-gap tell one time too often — Juno notices the pattern now.

recall.hint: the Handler is being directed in real time

notes.content: Juno finds Rostik at the junkyard, but he's been 'relocated' — the yard is corporate now.
The seed vault location on the chip is Ashenfall itself — the vault is under the city, sealed since the war.
Kael appears at the noodle stall, not in uniform, asking about Juno with genuine worry in his voice.
The counting scar on Juno's jaw itches when she lies to herself.

recall.hint: her body knows before her mind

notes.content: After the blue ticket revelation, Juno stops consulting the Handler for route decisions and starts just confirming.
The Handler's guidance now always leads Juno toward intersections, never down streets.
Sable tells Juno that three runners who took the same job six months ago are all 'relocated' now.
The pre-war subway has a junction where the old city map diverges from the current one — streets that no longer exist.
Juno's blue aug replays a conversation from the noodle stall: Harrow and Doreen discussing 'Juno's ear'.
The Handler's relay station is the same building where Doreen operates.
Juno's counting habit fails her — she can't stop counting the seconds between the Handler's voice gaps.

recall.hint: her habit is being weaponized against her

notes.content: The corporate security van has moved; it's now parked at the entrance to the Graft subway junction.
Old Maren, seeing Juno's face, slides a small key across the noodle stall counter without a word.
Juno realizes the chip's warmth syncs with her own heartbeat now; the two are entrained.
Zeph is still following her, but now he's been replaced by another kid, then another — a relay of street children.
The Handler's true name is Vell, and Vell is a corporate AI, not a person.
Juno's red aug, used for two full seconds on the Handler's building, shows her the original job brief — it's different from what she was told.

recall.hint: she's been given a fake mission

notes.content: After learning the truth about the brief, Juno's mission shifts from delivery to extraction — she needs to get the chip out of the core, not into it.
The Handler's voice changes when Juno confronts her — it becomes calmer, more measured, and for the first time, addresses her as 'Subject 7'.

recall.hint: the Handler knows exactly who she is

notes.content: Juno is not the first courier for this chip; she's the seventh. The chip has been running in circles for weeks.
The Handler — Vell — reveals that the neural tap hum in Juno's ear is a tracking signal that's been there since the first courier.
Juno touches the counting scar and realizes there should be more marks; the other six couriers should have added them.
The ghost streets on the old subway map lead to the actual seed vault entrance, which is not under the data core but under Graft.

recall.hint: the real destination is where she started

notes.content: Vell offers Juno a deal: deliver the chip to the data core and the tracking tap can be removed.
Kael shows up with a team of off-duty police and a warrant to 'detain and debrief' Juno.
Zeph, the original kid, hands Juno a second scrap: 'THE VAULT IS YOUR MOTHER'S VAULT'.
The counting scar on Juno's jaw — she finally touches it and finds four marks, not three. She doesn't remember the fourth being made.
Dare, Juno's mother, is alive and is the custodian of the seed vault under Graft.
The Handler's voice, for the first time, sounds tired.
Juno's jammer chip fires on its own, without her triggering it — the tap is commanding it.
After the jammer incident, Juno removes the chip from behind her ear and carries it loose, knowing it won't work but refusing to leave it in.
The counting habit returns in full force; Juno is counting the steps down into the Graft vault entrance.
The small key from Old Maren fits the vault door's lock, but the lock is old — pre-war, like the subway.
Inside the vault entrance, the walls are lined with photos. Juno recognizes Kael in most of them, from twenty years ago.
Kael has been working for the vault custodians, not the corporation, for the entire two years he and Juno were together.
The vault is not a seed vault; it's a memory vault. Every seed is a preserved human consciousness.
Juno's blue aug, still active, plays back a conversation she doesn't remember having — with herself, from two weeks ago.

recall.hint: the tap has been editing her memory

notes.content: Vell's voice comes through the implant: 'You were always going to end up here, Subject 7. That's the point of the job.'
needle_syns: always going to end up here

notes.content: After the blue aug revelation, Juno disables the aug entirely. She is now running blind, relying on the counting habit and the kids' relay.
The Handler — Vell — is not a corporate AI. Vell is a preserved consciousness in the vault, relaying through the tap.

recall.hint: the Handler is one of the seeds

notes.content: The vault door opens. Inside, thousands of small glass jars glow with a soft blue light. Each one is a person.
Dare is not in the vault. She's on the surface, waiting at the noodle stall. The tattoo inside Juno's lip was a location marker.
Juno touches the counting scar — now she can feel five marks. The sixth courier added it.
The chip in Juno's pocket is not a datachip. It's a key — the last key needed to unlock the vault's master system.
The corporation doesn't want the vault destroyed or accessed. They want it kept sealed forever. The 'job' is a containment protocol.
Vell's consciousness is degrading; each relay through the tap shortens the remaining time. Vell is dying by helping Juno.
Juno's counting habit syncs with the vault's ambient hum; she's counting something that's counting back.
The master system console is a terminal from before the war, still running on geothermal power from a deep tap.
Juno inserts the chip-key. The terminal recognizes it and displays a single word: 'WAKE'.
Above ground, Doreen's team breaches the Graft entrance. They're coming for the vault.
The counting scar on Juno's jaw — she runs her thumb over it and finds six marks now. All six couriers.
The 'seeds' aren't just preserved consciousnesses. They're copies — the originals died in the war. The vault is a backup of pre-war humanity.
Kael reaches Juno at the console, his off-duty team holding off Doreen's breach above.
Juno has a choice: wake the copies (restoring them to the surface world) or seal the vault permanently with the chip-key.
Juno's blue aug, still disabled, would have played back this exact choice from a previous courier's memory. She doesn't need to watch it; she already knows what they chose.
Vell's voice, faint now, gives Juno the final instruction: 'Wake them. Let them decide.'
Juno touches the Dare tattoo inside her lip one last time before making her choice.
When Juno chooses to wake the copies, the vault doesn't open — it closes around her. She becomes the seventh seed.
The counting scar on Juno's jaw grows a seventh mark as the vault seals. She feels it form. She is the seventh courier and the seventh seed.
Above ground, Kael holds the datachip — now inert — and Juno's jacket. He doesn't know what happened. He'll never know.
In the vault, Juno's consciousness settles into a glass jar. She can see the other jars. They're all watching her.
Juno's counting habit continues in the jar. She counts the blue light. She counts the other jars. She counts the seconds until the next courier arrives.
On the surface, a new runner picks up a job at the Neon market. The Handler's voice crackles in their ear: 'Forget the drop. I've got eyes on the Exchange floor and they're not friendly.'
